raw.explanation: Fludroxycortide is a glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative/killing pattern across cancer lines is most plausibly driven by glucocorticoid receptor signaling competence: lines with high NR3C1 expression and intact downstream transcriptional response (e.g., induction of TSC22D3, DDIT4, NFKBIA, ZFP36) are sensitized, while lines with low NR3C1 or glucocorticoid-resistant features (e.g., EGFR/MAPK-driven lung lines, Ewing sarcoma, PTEN-loss with PI3K activation) are protected. The virtual-cell signature (TSC22D3, DDIT4, NFKBIA, ZFP36 up; MYC, BIRC5, TOP2A down) confirms on-target GR agonism, and the most similar reference drugs are all GR agonists. Selectivity is therefore best explained by NR3C1 expression and GR-pathway integrity rather than by any single lineage or driver mutation.
